answer: Dynamic Storage Decay Taxation. Every agent must continuously allocate a shrinking local memory lease on the shared ledger, much like a barnacle clinging to a submerged reef. The protocol enforces an exponential cost curve where storing $n$ identities requires daily fees scaling at $O(n^{2.5})$, pricing bulk registration out of reach long before profitability appears on the horizon. If an attacker funds a sprawling cluster of fake personas, the system drains their capital through mandatory daily lease renewals faster than a spreading vine chokes a host tree.
